jobs.title: Supply Chain & Procurement Lead, GPU Infrastructure
jobs.description:
SUPPLY CHAIN & PROCUREMENT LEAD, GPU INFRASTRUCTURE




ABOUT PARASAIL

Parasail builds inference infrastructure for open-weight AI models. Behind one API, we bring together distributed GPU capacity and optimize how workloads run across it, helping customers access reliable, high-performance inference without managing the underlying infrastructure.

We’re building the team that sources, deploys, and operates the hardware behind that platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll own the supplier relationships, purchasing, and supply planning that support Parasail’s GPU infrastructure—from identifying hardware needs and securing supply through delivery, replacements, and lifecycle management.

This is an early role with responsibility for both strategy and execution. You’ll negotiate with vendors, manage purchasing and delivery commitments, resolve shortages, and build visibility into equipment availability and cost. Working closely with engineering, finance, and our Data Center Deployment & Operations TPM, you’ll ensure purchasing decisions support real deployment needs.

Initially, you’ll work directly with suppliers, hardware manufacturers, distributors, and logistics partners to get things done. As Parasail grows, you’ll build the processes, systems, and team needed to support a larger infrastructure footprint.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own supplier relationships. Evaluate and manage hardware manufacturers, distributors, integrators, and logistics partners. Establish clear expectations for pricing, availability, quality, delivery, and support.

 - Lead sourcing and purchasing. Run vendor evaluations and requests for quotes, negotiate commercial terms, and manage purchases for GPUs, servers, networking equipment, racks, spares, and supporting hardware.

 - Build the supply plan. Translate capacity requirements and deployment schedules into purchasing plans. Account for equipment already available, supplier lead times, configuration changes, and budget constraints.

 - Drive delivery commitments. Track orders from placement through manufacturing, shipment, and receipt. Resolve delays and discrepancies, and develop alternatives when supply puts a deployment at risk.

 - Partner on technical decisions. Work with engineering to confirm specifications, evaluate substitutions, and understand how hardware choices affect cost, availability, compatibility, and deployment timing.

 - Manage inventory and lifecycle. Maintain visibility into equipment that is ordered, in transit, in storage, deployed, or awaiting repair. Coordinate spares, warranties, returns, replacements, and end-of-life disposition with operations.

 - Balance cost and availability. Evaluate total acquisition costs, payment terms, inventory exposure, and the cost of delayed capacity. Present clear purchasing recommendations to finance and leadership.

 - Build procurement systems and controls. Establish practical workflows for purchase approvals, order tracking, inventory reconciliation, and invoice discrepancies. Automate repetitive work and keep records reliable as volume grows.

 - Keep supply and deployment aligned. Provide dependable equipment milestones to the deployment TPM. Surface shortages, supplier risks, and decisions early, with recovery options and accountable owners.

 - Build the function. Define supplier performance measures, improve purchasing and planning practices, and help hire and develop the team as demand grows.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Experience owning hardware procurement, supply chain, or materials planning in cloud infrastructure, data centers, electronics, or another complex hardware environment.

 - Direct responsibility for supplier relationships, commercial negotiations, purchasing decisions, and delivery commitments.

 - Experience managing supply against changing demand, including shortages, long lead times, configuration changes, and excess inventory.

 - An understanding of server and infrastructure hardware sufficient to work effectively with engineering on specifications and purchasing tradeoffs.

 - Strong analytical skills and experience building planning tools, procurement workflows, or inventory reporting.

 - A track record of resolving problems across suppliers, logistics providers, finance, and technical teams.

 - Comfort handling detailed execution while building a more scalable operating process.

 - Clear communication about costs, commitments, risks, and decisions.


HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - Sourcing GPUs, servers, networking equipment, or integrated rack systems.

 - Working with OEMs, ODMs, contract manufacturers, and hardware distributors.

 - Supporting GPU infrastructure deployments or introducing new hardware platforms.

 - Coordinating international shipments with logistics and trade-compliance specialists.

 - Managing hardware warranties, returns, spare-parts planning, and lifecycle transitions.

 - Building or leading a procurement, supply planning, or hardware operations team.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Parasail has dependable access to the equipment needed for its deployment plans. Supplier commitments and inventory records are trustworthy, purchasing decisions balance cost and availability, and supply risks are addressed before they delay capacity. The systems and team you build allow the function to scale with the business.

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships Manager
jobs.description:
STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS MANAGER




ABOUT PARASAIL

Parasail is building the inference cloud for AI-native companies. We bring together GPU capacity across infrastructure providers into a unified platform, helping customers deploy and scale production AI workloads with the performance, reliability, and economics they need—without managing the underlying infrastructure.

We’re expanding our fleet and building the relationships that support our next stage of growth. Partnerships are central to that work, shaping our access to compute and our opportunities across the global AI ecosystem.




THE ROLE

We’re hiring our first dedicated Strategic Partnerships Manager to own and expand relationships with GPU capacity providers, hardware manufacturers, and AI model companies.

You’ll inherit an active provider portfolio and take ownership of GPU rental relationships, capacity sourcing, and commercial negotiations. Alongside that work, you’ll develop strategic partnerships across the AI ecosystem, working closely with company leadership.

This is a hands-on role with meaningful ownership from the start. As the business grows, you’ll have the opportunity to shape and help build out the partnerships function.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own GPU provider relationships. Manage regular touchpoints, capacity availability, pricing, and rental negotiations to secure preferred access to compute as our fleet grows.

 - Expand our supply options. Source, qualify, and onboard new capacity providers to diversify supply and improve commercial terms.

 - Build hardware partnerships. Develop relationships with established manufacturers and emerging silicon and accelerator companies, positioning Parasail for early access to new hardware and preferred partnership terms.

 - Develop model-provider partnerships. Build strategic relationships with AI model companies in the US and internationally, identifying commercial and ecosystem opportunities.

 - Track commercial performance. Maintain a clear view of capacity pipeline, provider health, and rental economics against our fleet growth and financial plans.

 - Represent Parasail. Participate in partner meetings and industry events domestically and internationally, pursuing new opportunities as the business evolves.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3–6+ years in partnerships, business development, strategic sourcing, consulting, or account management, ideally in cloud, infrastructure, semiconductors, or AI.

 - Strong communication skills and confidence managing senior external relationships, from GPU cloud operators and hardware executives to AI model teams.

 - Commercial judgment: you can model deal economics, weigh tradeoffs, and negotiate agreements that hold up over time.

 - Familiarity with the GPU and accelerator landscape and cloud compute economics, or the ability to learn the market quickly.

 - Comfort working across geographies and cultures.

 - The initiative, organization, and follow-through to manage ambiguous problems independently while collaborating closely with a small team.

Nice to have: Existing relationships with GPU providers, hardware manufacturers, or AI labs; experience working with China-based technology companies; professional working proficiency in Mandarin; or an MBA or comparable business training.




WHY JOIN PARASAIL

You’ll own relationships that directly influence our capacity, economics, and growth. You’ll work closely with leadership on consequential commercial decisions and help build a partnerships function with increasing scope as the company scales.
